spec_family.name: Exterior Fence Repaint (Stain & Paint)
spec_family.description: Condition-assessment-driven repaint specification for previously stained or painted exterior wood fences (cedar, pressure-treated pine). Covers 4 substrate states (SS_EXT_STAINED_SEMI, SS_EXT_STAINED_SOLID, SS_EXT_WEATHERED, SS_EXT_PEELING) with 3-level condition scale (GOOD/FAIR/POOR) driving prep intensity. Recoat compatibility matrix is the critical RP constraint — penetrating stains can only recoat over penetrating stains; solid stain/paint can recoat over solid stain or paint. Coating_type (transparent/semi_transparent/solid_stain/paint) constrained by substrate_state. QT2-QT3 only (utilitarian surface). Spray_backbrush is production standard with mandatory back-brushing for penetrating stains. Two-sided painting (both sides of fence) — PaintScope delivers final SF after (LF x Height x 2) and fence_style multiplier. Chemical restoration module for weathered fences (3-step: strip, brighten, rinse — 12-24 hr dry, separate mobilization). Post base rot assessment is RP-specific HARD STOP. RRP conditional for pre-1978 properties. Paint recoat carries LEAST RECOMMENDED warning (moisture-driven peeling risk). Single paintable item (ITM_FENCE_FIELD, SF). No height modifier — all ground-level work.

includes: Condition assessment — identify existing coating type (penetrating stain, solid stain, paint)
Coating adhesion test (film-forming coatings only)
Wood moisture content testing (MC <=19% untreated, <=25% PT pine — HARD STOP)
Post base rot assessment at grade line (rot = HARD STOP)
Mildew and algae assessment
Pressure wash (1,000-1,500 PSI — lower pressure for cedar)
Mildew eradication treatment (conditional)
Scrape loose/failing coating (peeling condition)
Feather-edge sanding of scraped areas (mandatory after scraping)
Light scuff sand for adhesion on sound solid stain/paint
Chemical wood restoration for weathered fences (3-step: alkaline strip, acid brighten, rinse — 12-24 hr dry)
Condition-driven primer — stain-blocking (cedar bare wood), standard exterior (PT pine bare wood)
Stain recoat — penetrating (transparent, semi-transparent) or solid body
Paint recoat — exterior acrylic latex (LEAST RECOMMENDED)
Second coat application (QT3 solid stain and paint only)
Both-sides application sequencing (Side A -> equipment move -> Side B)
Gate hardware removal and reinstallation
Landscape protection along fence base (both sides, LF-based)
Hardscape protection for adjacent driveways/patios/walkways
Siding protection at fence-to-house tie-in
Neighbor-side overspray protection (spray method only)
Vehicle overspray protection (spray method only)
EPA RRP lead-safe containment (pre_1978 conditional)
Final walkthrough inspection and touch-up
Paint risk warning documentation (when coating_type = paint)

Out of scope — maintenance-free by design

configuration_dimensions.description: PRIMARY dimension — existing coating condition drives prep module selection and recoat compatibility.
configuration_dimensions.notes: SS_EXT_STAINED_SEMI = serviceable penetrating stain. SS_EXT_STAINED_SOLID = serviceable solid stain or paint film. SS_EXT_WEATHERED = UV-degraded, coating largely eroded. SS_EXT_PEELING = film-forming coating actively lifting.

configuration_dimensions.description: SECONDARY dimension — drives prep intensity modifier (FAC_FERP_CONDITION).
configuration_dimensions.notes: GOOD = serviceable coating, minimal prep. FAIR = moderate wear/weathering, standard prep. POOR = significant failure, heavy prep. Maps to 1.0x / 1.5x / 2.0x prep modifier.

configuration_dimensions.description: TERTIARY dimension — constrained by substrate_state recoat compatibility matrix.
configuration_dimensions.notes: Semi-transparent is default recoat for penetrating stain substrates. Recoat compatibility: penetrating -> penetrating only. Solid stain -> solid stain or paint. Paint -> paint only.

configuration_dimensions.description: Coat count driver. Fence is utilitarian — QT2 and QT3 only.
configuration_dimensions.notes: QT2 = economy single coat (appropriate for penetrating stain recoat). QT3 = standard (2 coats for solid stain/paint recoat). QT4/QT5 excluded.

configuration_dimensions.description: Primary application technique for stain/paint coats.
configuration_dimensions.notes: Spray_backbrush is production standard (2-person crew). Back-brushing MANDATORY for penetrating stains. Brush for detail, small jobs, split rail. Roll excluded for RP.

configuration_dimensions.description: Wood species. Drives tannin management and rate modifier.
configuration_dimensions.notes: PT pine ~65% of fences. Cedar ~30%. Cedar requires tannin-blocking primer when bare wood is exposed under peeling coating.

configuration_dimensions.description: Boolean flag for pre-1978 property. Triggers EPA RRP lead-safe requirements.
configuration_dimensions.notes: Lead paint on fences is uncommon but possible. RRP containment and wet scraping methods when positive.

paintable_items.name: Fence Field Surface (panels, boards, posts, rails, gates — both sides)
paintable_items.counting_rules: Net fence field surface area in square feet. PaintScope delivers FINAL SF after (LF x Height x 2) and fence_style geometric multiplier. Includes both sides, all panels, posts, gates, and rails. Spec receives and uses final SF as-is.
paintable_items.notes: Reused from NC spec. Single paintable item. Simplest item model among exterior wood specs.

valid_input_states.notes: SS_EXT_STAINED_SEMI = serviceable penetrating stain (transparent or semi-transparent). SS_EXT_STAINED_SOLID = serviceable solid stain or paint (film-forming). SS_EXT_WEATHERED = UV-degraded, coating largely eroded, wood grayed. SS_EXT_PEELING = film-forming coating actively lifting from substrate.

output_state.notes: Output state varies by coating_type. Penetrating stains -> SS_EXT_STAINED_SEMI. Solid stain -> SS_EXT_STAINED_SOLID. Paint -> SS_EXT_PAINTED_SATIN.

recoat_compatibility_matrix.description: CRITICAL RP CONSTRAINT — which coating types can be applied over which existing substrate states.

SS_EXT_STAINED_SEMI.notes: Penetrating stain can only be recoated with penetrating stain. Cannot apply film-forming over penetrating stain without full stripping.

SS_EXT_STAINED_SOLID.notes: Film-forming coating can be recoated with film-forming. Cannot apply penetrating stain over film — film prevents absorption.

SS_EXT_WEATHERED.notes: Weathered wood (coating eroded) — essentially bare wood after chemical restoration. All coating types allowed.

SS_EXT_PEELING.notes: Peeling film-forming coating — after scraping, may have mix of bare wood and adhered coating. Only film-forming recoats allowed (need film to bridge transitions).

protection_zones_required.notes: Landscaping along fence base on BOTH sides. Drop cloth/plastic. Extends 2-3 ft from fence base (4-6 ft for spray).
Walkways, driveways, patios along fence line. Stain on concrete is extremely difficult to remove.
House siding where fence attaches. Upgrade to full cover for spray.
Vehicles within spray range. Full plastic cover. Spray method only.
Neighbor's side of fence. Drop cloth along neighbor side fence base. Spray method only.

material_systems_summary.name: Penetrating Stain Recoat
material_systems_summary.notes: Direct recoat over serviceable penetrating stain. No primer.

material_systems_summary.name: Solid Body Stain Recoat
material_systems_summary.notes: Film-forming solid stain recoat. Primer if bare wood exposed.

material_systems_summary.name: Alkyd Stain-Blocking Primer
material_systems_summary.notes: MANDATORY on bare cedar exposed under peeling coating + film-forming topcoat.

material_systems_summary.name: Standard Exterior Acrylic Primer
material_systems_summary.notes: Standard exterior primer for bare PT pine + paint recoat.

material_systems_summary.name: Fence Cleaner / Stripper (Alkaline)
material_systems_summary.notes: Reused from NC. Chemical restoration step 1.

material_systems_summary.name: Wood Brightener (Oxalic / Citric Acid)
material_systems_summary.notes: Reused from NC. Chemical restoration step 2.

Power wash, mildew treat, scrape, feather sand, scuff sand, dust cleanup
Coat 1 — stain (3 types) or paint, by method (spray_backbrush or brush)
Coat 2 — QT3 solid stain or paint only
Final inspect, touch-up, gate hardware reinstall, protection teardown, tool cleanup

factor_modifiers.notes: Prep tasks only. GOOD=baseline, FAIR=moderate wear, POOR=significant failure.
Prep tasks involving paint disturbance. Binary gate.
Application tasks only. Semi-transparent is baseline.
Both prep and application tasks. Cedar is softer, absorbs more.

production_summary.prep_stack_note: 4.40x in extreme RRP scenario (POOR x RRP x cedar) — recommend T&M billing
production_summary.notes: No FAC_EXT_ACCESS — all fence work is ground-level. Rates reused from NC with RP adjustments for assessment and condition-driven prep tasks.

compatibility_rules.name: Recoat compatibility — penetrating over penetrating only
compatibility_rules.condition: substrate_state = SS_EXT_STAINED_SEMI AND coating_type IN (solid_stain, paint)
compatibility_rules.action: BLOCK — cannot apply film-forming coating over penetrating stain without full stripping. Select transparent or semi_transparent for recoat.

compatibility_rules.name: Recoat compatibility — no penetrating over film-forming
compatibility_rules.condition: substrate_state = SS_EXT_STAINED_SOLID AND coating_type IN (transparent, semi_transparent)
compatibility_rules.action: BLOCK — cannot apply penetrating stain over solid stain or paint. Film prevents absorption. Select solid_stain or paint for recoat.

compatibility_rules.name: Recoat compatibility — peeling requires film-forming
compatibility_rules.condition: substrate_state = SS_EXT_PEELING AND coating_type IN (transparent, semi_transparent)
compatibility_rules.action: BLOCK — peeling surface has mix of bare wood and adhered coating. Penetrating stain will not perform on patched/mixed surface. Select solid_stain or paint.

compatibility_rules.name: MC hard stop
compatibility_rules.action: HARD STOP — do not apply stain or paint. Retest after 24 hr dry period.

compatibility_rules.name: Post rot hard stop
compatibility_rules.condition: Post base rot detected during assessment
compatibility_rules.action: HARD STOP for affected posts — refer to fence contractor. Remaining fence may proceed. Document rotted posts in project record.

compatibility_rules.name: Paint risk warning mandatory
compatibility_rules.action: Document moisture-driven peeling risk warning with customer acknowledgment. Paint is LEAST RECOMMENDED for wood fences.

compatibility_rules.name: Back-brushing mandatory for spray penetrating stains
compatibility_rules.condition: application_method = spray_backbrush AND coating_type IN (transparent, semi_transparent, solid_stain)
compatibility_rules.action: Spray-only is PROHIBITED for penetrating stains. Spray must be followed immediately by back-brushing.

compatibility_rules.name: Cedar tannin-blocking primer when bare wood exposed
compatibility_rules.condition: substrate_material = cedar AND substrate_state = SS_EXT_PEELING AND coating_type IN (solid_stain, paint)
compatibility_rules.action: Activate SYS_EXT_FERP_PRIMER_STAIN_BLOCK. Cedar tannins bleed through film-forming coatings.

compatibility_rules.name: Chemical restoration requires separate mobilization
compatibility_rules.action: Chemical restoration requires 12-24 hr dry time before staining. Plan separate mobilization day.

compatibility_rules.name: Penetrating stains skip primer entirely
compatibility_rules.action: Do NOT apply primer. Primer seals wood and prevents stain penetration.

compatibility_rules.name: QT2 single coat — penetrating stains only
compatibility_rules.condition: quality_tier = QT2 AND coating_type IN (solid_stain, paint)
compatibility_rules.action: Warn — single coat solid stain or paint may not provide adequate coverage. QT3 (2 coats) recommended for film-forming coatings.

compatibility_rules.name: Transparent not recommended for PT pine
compatibility_rules.action: Warn — greenish PT chemical color shows through clear sealer. Semi-transparent recommended.

round_configurations.name: Penetrating Stain Recoat — 1 Coat
round_configurations.notes: Single coat penetrating recoat. No primer. No second coat. Simplest RP configuration.

round_configurations.name: Solid Stain Recoat — 1 Coat (QT2 Economy)
round_configurations.notes: Single coat solid stain economy recoat. Primer conditional on exposed bare wood.

round_configurations.name: Solid Stain Recoat — 2 Coats (QT3 Standard)
round_configurations.notes: Two-coat solid stain recoat. Standard configuration. Primer conditional on bare wood.

round_configurations.name: Paint Recoat — Primer + 1-2 Finish Coats
round_configurations.notes: LEAST RECOMMENDED. Primer conditional on exposed bare wood. QT2=1 coat, QT3=2 coats.

variants.notes: MOST COMMON RP scenario. Serviceable PT pine fence, semi-transparent spray recoat. Minimal prep — wash and recoat.
Cedar fence semi-transparent recoat. Good condition. Wash and recoat.
Weathered fence restoration + recoat. Chemical restoration module activated. Separate mobilization day.
Worst-case stain RP. Peeling cedar — scrape + feather sand + tannin-blocking primer + 2 coat solid stain.
LEAST RECOMMENDED. Peeling paint on PT pine. Full scrape + primer + 2 paint coats. Maximum protection. Mandatory risk warning.
Small fence or split rail. Brush recoat. Minimal protection (no spray overspray).
Solid stain recoat on fair-condition PT pine. Scuff sand + 2 coat solid stain. No primer (no bare wood).
Economy cedar maintenance recoat — clear sealer over existing penetrating stain.

hard_stops.action: STOP — do not apply coating. Retest after 24 hr dry period.
STOP — refer rotted posts to fence contractor. Remaining fence may proceed.

risk_flags.name: Recoat incompatibility — penetrating over film-forming
risk_flags.description: Cannot apply penetrating stain over solid stain or paint. Film prevents absorption. Most common RP specification error.
risk_flags.mitigation: Engine must enforce recoat compatibility matrix. UI must disable incompatible selections.

risk_flags.name: Paint on wood fence — moisture-driven peeling
risk_flags.description: Paint recoat carries same moisture-driven peeling risk as NC. Fences are fully exposed to weather on BOTH faces.
risk_flags.mitigation: Use penetrating stains when possible. If paint: high permeability formulation, document risk warning.

risk_flags.name: Post base rot — structural failure risk
risk_flags.description: Rotted posts at grade line are structural — painting over rot masks the damage and accelerates failure.
risk_flags.mitigation: HARD STOP. Rot probe assessment mandatory. Document and refer to fence contractor.

risk_flags.name: Cedar tannin bleed through exposed bare wood
risk_flags.description: Peeling coating on cedar exposes bare wood — tannins will bleed through film-forming topcoat without proper primer.
risk_flags.mitigation: Tannin-blocking primer (alkyd/shellac) mandatory on bare cedar + solid stain or paint topcoat.

adjacent_surfaces.notes: House siding at fence-to-house tie-in. Protection required at junction.
Posts integral to fence — stained as part of field pass.
Gates stained with fence field. Hardware removal/reinstall is separate task.

sequencing_notes.production_sequence: Assess -> Setup/Protect -> Power Wash -> Prep (condition-driven) -> Chemical Restore (weathered only, separate mobilization) -> Prime (conditional) -> Apply Coat 1 -> Apply Coat 2 (QT3 solid/paint only) -> Final Inspect -> Touch-Up -> Cleanup
sequencing_notes.both_sides_workflow: Side A protection -> Side A application -> Equipment move -> Side B protection -> Side B application. Both sides complete coat 1 before either side gets coat 2.
sequencing_notes.protection_sequence: Landscape (both sides) -> Hardscape -> Siding tie -> Neighbor property (spray only) -> Vehicle (spray only) -> Gate hardware -> Coating work -> Protection teardown -> Equipment cleanup
sequencing_notes.key_prohibitions: NO penetrating stain over film-forming (recoat compatibility). NO film-forming over penetrating without stripping. NO spray-only for penetrating stains (back-brush mandatory). NO staining at MC > threshold. NO painting over rotted posts.

maintenance_cycles.notes: Shortest cycle. Annual recoat typical. Clean and recoat.
Professional standard. Clean and recoat. Sun-exposed faces sooner.
Longer cycle on vertical surfaces. May need sanding at recoat time.
Longest theoretical but HIGHEST FAILURE RISK. Peeling often within 2-3 years.

cross_spec_boundaries.notes: NC sibling spec. Different prep (no condition assessment, no scraping), different substrate states.
Different substrate, primer, and coating chemistry.
Post replacement, board replacement, structural repair.

relationships.notes: RP sibling to SF_FENCE_EXT_v1 (NC). Shares stain-based architecture, coating_type dimension, single paintable item, and fence-specific protection zones. Key departures: condition assessment module, recoat compatibility matrix, condition_scale modifier, substrate_state replaces wood_condition as primary dimension.

research_corrections.original_claim: Metal fences (wrought iron) could be included via fence_material dimension
research_corrections.corrected_to: Metal fences EXCLUDED — different substrate, primer, and coating chemistry.
Roll EXCLUDED for RP — not practical for weathered/previously coated vertical fence surfaces.

change_log.author: SpecFactory
change_log.changes: Initial draft spec for exterior fence repaint. RP sibling to SF_FENCE_EXT_v1 (NC). Context prefix: FERP. Key features: 4 substrate states (stained_semi/stained_solid/weathered/peeling), 3-level condition scale (GOOD/FAIR/POOR), recoat compatibility matrix (critical RP constraint), 4 coating types (transparent/semi_transparent/solid_stain/paint), QT2-QT3 only, 2 application methods (spray_backbrush/brush — roll excluded for RP), 2 substrate materials (cedar/PT pine), single paintable item (ITM_FENCE_FIELD SF), 35 tasks across 8 modules (31 binary + 4 qt_conditional), 7 material systems (2 stain + 1 paint + 2 primer + 2 prep chemical), 4 factor modifiers (condition/RRP/coating_type/substrate_type) with stacking partition, 4 round configurations, 5 protection zones (reused from NC), 14 consumables, 12 compatibility rules, 8 variants, 14 PaintScope inputs, 2 hard stops (MC threshold, post rot). Assessment module is RP-NEW (5 tasks). Chemical restoration module carried from NC (8 tasks). Max prep stack 4.40x (extreme RRP scenario — T&M recommended). Max coating stack 1.43x. No height modifier — ground-level work.
